The twelfth beta of CoSky 8.0, still for developers to try. It fixes five problems a review of the whole project found, from a cleanup that could delete a namespace to a Redis log that could outgrow its byte limit. The stable release is still 6.x, on the [`v6`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/tree/v6) branch.

There is no compatibility promise before `8.0.0-rc.1`, which freezes what [`CONTRIBUTING.md`](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md#releases-and-versioning) lists.

## Try it

[Getting Started](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/getting-started) takes a few minutes: a server in development mode, a Spring Boot application that reads a Config and registers, and another that finds it.

```bash
docker run -p 8080:8080 -p 9090:9090 ahoowang/cosky:8.0.0-beta.12 --dev
```

What helps most is still what we could only try on one machine: Redis Sentinel or Cluster of your own with a failover, an OIDC provider other than Keycloak, moving a 6.x installation with `cosky-migrate`, and a real network. [Tell us](https://github.com/Ahoo-Wang/CoSky/issues/new/choose) what breaks or surprises you.

## Fixed

- **The account cleanup could delete a Namespace.** The server removes the ServiceAccount and RoleBinding a namespace came with once the namespace is gone. It deleted any `_system` object that carried their two labels, whatever its kind. Someone allowed to write a Namespace but not to delete one could label it so that the cleanup deleted it, past the checks of a deletion. Its data stayed without an object, and the lease reaper no longer reaped its Instances. The cleanup now deletes only the account and binding it made. (#1290)
- **Creating a ServiceAccount again could bring back the tokens of the one deleted.** A create with `If-None-Match: *`, served by a replica that had not yet seen the deletion, copied the old account's tokens into the new one. Deleting an account to revoke a leaked token, and creating it again, could leave that token working. A new account now starts without tokens. (#1290)
- **The Redis log could grow far past its byte limit.** The log is trimmed after each write by entries and by bytes, but each write removed at most a few dozen entries. Large Configs written over many small Instance events took the log to several times `cosky.watch.window-bytes`, up to about 1 GiB. Each write now removes at least as many bytes as it adds. (#1290)
- **One resource could be too large for every watcher.** Only a Config's content was limited in size. An Instance or Role made large through a field without a limit of its own reached every watcher as a message larger than gRPC takes by default, and ended its stream on every reconnect. A resource larger than 2 MiB serialized, the most one message holds, is now refused. (#1290)
- **One registration the server refused kept the others from coming back.** When a lease was lost, or Instances were lost while it lived on, the client stopped at the first registration the server refused, such as one whose service it may no longer write. The others were not registered again, and the renewal stream restarted every few seconds. They now come back, and the refused one is tried again with each renewal. (#1290)

## Upgrading from beta.11

- Nothing changes: the gRPC API, the protos, REST, the data in Redis and the properties. Applications stay on Spring Boot 4.2.0 and Spring Cloud 2026.0.0. `cosky-migrate` and the Dashboard come with this release.
- A write of a resource larger than 2 MiB serialized is now refused with `INVALID_ARGUMENT`. Configs within their content limit are not affected.
- beta.11 reached GitHub Packages only in part (`cosky-api` and `cosky-bom`); use Maven Central for it, or this release.

## Known limits

- **Tried on one laptop, not in a data center:** the Cluster and Sentinel failovers, the scale and the emulated network on the [Performance](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/performance) page. OIDC was tried with Keycloak 26 only.
- **On Sentinel,** while a master that hangs still holds the connection hints come on, each replica reads every namespace every second instead. A write then takes up to a second to reach watchers.
- **At rest, each replica reads each namespace once a second,** in case a hint was lost. On one Redis, 5,000 namespaces and three replicas took 30% of its CPU. A Cluster, or a longer `cosky.store.redis.tail-poll-interval`, lowers it.
- **Writes over a lossy network:** where 1% of packets are lost, a write's p99 is above 200 ms, as TCP waits to resend a lost packet.
- **A replica cut off from Redis on its own** goes on serving what it last knew, and stays ready. [Deployment](https://cosky.ahoo.me/guide/deployment) shows how to notice.
- **A late Namespace creation that takes a write before it is undone** stays, without an object, and the server logs an error. That takes a write in the round trip between making the namespace and dropping it.
- **Removing every CoSky import at once** leaves their properties in place. A refresh that loaded no CoSky Config at all is not taken as one that ran the imports, so that nothing is dropped by mistake.
- **The server does not stop an account from granting itself roles** it may write; see the security guide.
